sentences.text:
The present applicants who have been arraigned as an accused have preferred the applications under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicants on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No. 11208044250647 of 2025 registered with Pradhyumannagar Police Station, Rajkot City for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 465,
467, 468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code before filing of the charge-sheet.

R/CR.MA/24745/2025 ORDER DA  
4.

It would appear that the applicants had originally approached this Court by preferring Criminal Misc. Application No. 22816 of 2025 and 22935 of 2025 respectively seeking for regular bail and vide an order dated 06.11.2025, this Court had permitted the applicants to withdraw the applications with liberty to approach the learned Trial Court after chare- sheet is filed.
5.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Application No. 22816 of 2025 and 22935 of 2025
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
It would appear in this regard that the applicants thereafter had invoked jurisdiction of this Court under Section 539 of the BNSS and whereas vide an order dated 21.11.2025 in Criminal Misc.
Application ( Quashing and Set Aide FIR/Order) No. 24264 of 2025 learned Co- ordinate Bench had been pleased to protect the applicants inter alia by directing that the charge- sheet shall not be filed without prior permission of this Court.

It is also pointed out to this Court that in the interregnum,
that is vide an order dated 10.11.2025, a learned Co-ordinate Bench of this Court had protected some of the co-accused having similar role in an application preferred for grant of anticipatory bail.

6. Considering such a situation, it is requested by learned Advocate that since charge sheet would not be filed by the Investigating Officer in view of the order passed by the learned Co-ordinate Bench, and having regard to the change in circumstances since co-accused having considered for being enlarged on anticipatory bail this Court may consider the case of the applicants and release them on regular bail.

 R/CR.MA/24745/2025 ORDER

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Present applications have been vehemently opposed by learned APP on behalf of respondent- State who would submit that the present applicants, having approached the Bench taking up quashing matters and receiving an order of charge-sheet not being filed, may not be permitted to be used by the applicants themselves in the present applications more particularly since they had withdrawn the applications after a full-fledged hearing.
8.

This Court has heard learned Advocates for the respective parties and perused the FIR as well as order passed by learned Session Court as well as affidavit filed by the investigating officer before the learned Trial Court.

9. This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
8.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has also considered the following aspects:

(i) Though the facts reflect, a complicated issue more particularly the complication having arisen at the behest of the present applicants themselves, yet to this Court having regard to the fact that a learned Co-ordinate Bench has considered the case of co-accused for enlargement on anticipatory bail the case of the applicants also deserves to be reconsidered.
(ii) Since it appears that the allegations levelled against the co- accused who had been enlarged on anticipatory bail, having similar role as alleged to the present applicants.

Abdul Hussainbhai Dodhiya vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191241745/
3  R/CR.MA/24745/2025 ORDER

entities.text: Abdul Hussainbhai Dodhiya vs State Of Gujarat on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(iii) Since it is noticed by this Court that learned Bench has granted interim relief in favour of the present applicants in the nature of directing the investigating officer not to file the charge sheet therefore, the order of this Court whereby the present applicants were permitted to approach learned Trial Court after filing of the charge-sheet,
may result in the present applicants being prejudiced.

9. In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
10. Hence, the present applications are allowed.

11.
The Authorities will release the applicants only if they are not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to take appropriate action in the matter.
12. Bail bond to be executed before the lower court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions in accordance with law.

13. At the stage of trial, the trial court shall not be influenced by any observations of this Court which are of preliminary nature made at this stage, only for the purpose of considering the application of the applicant for being released on regular bail.
14. The applications are allowed in the aforesaid terms.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
